title: market_cap / price are ranked and threshold-compared across currencies as one number
repro: universe=custom, custom_symbols=[AAPL, RELIANCE.NS] -> results sort RELIANCE (~1.95e13 INR) above AAPL (~3.5e12 USD) under a header reading 'Market cap v'; likewise a criterion market_cap > 1e10 means $10B for sp500 and Rs 1,000 crore for india-all, with no unit shown in either the criterion input or the sort.
notes: Invariant held by a comment, not by the structure (APOSD 16/4): screener.py:41-43 states 'market_cap is in the LISTING currency' and nothing downstream carries that. D57 already fixed DISPLAY (ScreenerResultsTable.tsx:152/202 format per row.currency, 'Rs 1,293 must never render as $1,293') while the comparator one screen away does av - bv on the same field with row.currency in scope and unused. Consequence: for a product whose moat is data trust, the single number a screener exists to rank by is ranked wrong whenever a universe mixes currencies, and a saved screen (src/store/screener.ts:69-76 carries universe + criteria together) silently changes meaning by ~85x when its universe is switched. Smallest fix: (a) make the currency-denominated compare currency-aware in ONE place - carry a normalized market_cap_base alongside the listing value in ScreenerResultRow and sort/threshold on it; (b) until then, suffix the criterion input and the column header with the resolved universe's currency instead of leaving the unit implicit.

title: A NULL on any non-enrichment field silently fails the criterion instead of being itemized - the criteria path and the formula path have opposite null semantics
repro: criteria=[{field: pe_ratio, operator: lt, value: 20}] over nse-all -> rows whose stored pe_ratio is NULL are counted as evaluated-and-failed; coverage reads 'screened 2,675 of 2,675 - 0 unavailable'. The SAME predicate written as formula='pe < 20' itemizes those rows as missing_field:pe_ratio.
notes: Violates Consistency (APOSD 15) and the module's own SC-034 'zero silent drops' contract. _finalize's docstring (screener.py:683-685) promises 'NULL values for a field the screen references are itemized as skips', but the absent-check at 718-723 iterates needed_fields, which _enrichment_fields_needed (433-443) has already filtered down to fields where yahoo_batch_provider.field_needs_enrichment(f) is true - i.e. exactly the fields the v7 tier CAN supply are exempt from the honesty check, and _evaluate_criterion returns False for None (296-297). Consequence: the coverage line under-reports unavailability precisely for the most commonly-NULL v7 fields (pe_ratio, peg_ratio, dividend_yield on loss-making / non-dividend names), so 'no rows matched' is indistinguishable from 'we had no data'. Smallest fix: itemize on _criteria_fields(criteria, group) | formula_fields rather than on the enrichment subset.

title: Column sort reorders only the truncated result page while presenting itself as sorting the screen
repro: Run nse-all with limit=200 (store default), click the 'P/E' header ascending -> the table shows the lowest P/E among the 200 LARGEST names by market cap, not the lowest P/E in the universe. Nothing in the header, the count line, or a tooltip says so.
notes: Information leakage across the client/server boundary (APOSD 4/6): the server owns 'rank by market_cap then cut at limit' and the client owns 'rank by whatever the user clicked', and neither knows the other's half, so the composition means something no layer intends. For a screener this is the core flow - 'cheapest stock on the NSE' is a query the product visibly offers and silently cannot answer. Smallest fix: put sort_by/sort_dir on ScreenerRequest, apply it in apply_criteria before the limit cut (screener.py:397-399 already owns the comparator), and have the header re-run rather than re-sort; short of that, label the header 'sorting the top 200 by market cap'.

title: default_universe_for_region is dead code - the India-first screener default (FR-060) was never wired to anything
repro: design - grep over *.py/*.ts/*.tsx and sidecar/tests/ finds no call site for default_universe_for_region; the store hardcodes universe: 'sp500' at both init and reset, so an IN-region user opens the screener on the S&P 500.
notes: A general-purpose mechanism with zero clients (APOSD 5/17 - designing for a future that never arrived), plus a doc that asserts the feature exists: routers/screener.py:74-77 describes FR-060 region-aware default selection as living 'in services.screener.default_universe_for_region for the callers that must choose a default' - there are no such callers, so the only consumer of FR-060 is prose. Consequence: the flagship India positioning is contradicted by the panel's first frame, and the next maintainer reading the router docstring believes the behaviour is shipped. Smallest fix: initialise the store's universe from get_region() (via the existing /system region surface) on first mount, or delete the function and the docstring claim.

title: The screener_run agent tool returns an unbounded per-symbol skip ledger into the model's context
repro: agent calls screener_run(universe='india-all', criteria=[...]) and the run goes partial -> the tool result carries skip_details with one {symbol, reason} object per unevaluated symbol (up to ~5,000 for india-all), all of it serialized into the turn.
notes: Wrong layer choosing the abstraction (APOSD 6): the tool blanket-dumps the HTTP response shape. It is visibly aware of the problem - it overrides limit to 50 because 'the router default of 200 is fine for the UI but produces a chunky context blob for agents' (screener_tools.py:39-42) - and then ships a payload two orders of magnitude larger than the thing it capped. The UI already proves the right shape exists: ScreenerPanel.tsx:161-175 aggregates the ledger to '554 unavailable - 300 rate-limited . 254 missing roe'. Consequence: one partial india-all screen can consume most of an agent turn's context and burn the tokens the run was supposed to spend reasoning. Smallest fix: in _screener_run, replace skip_details with that same reason-count aggregate before returning.

title: Formula grammar has no type check: a boolean silently coerces to 1.0/0.0 inside arithmetic and min/max/abs
repro: formula='min(pe < 5, roe) > 0.5' validates ok (POST /screener/formula/validate -> ok:true) and evaluates True for pe=3/roe=0.9 and False for pe=99/roe=0.9 - the comparison silently became min(1.0, 0.9) > 0.5. Same for 'abs(pe_ratio > 3) > 0.5' and '(pe_ratio < 15) + 1 > 1.5'. Verified by running services.screener_formula directly against Fundamentals(pe_ratio=3.0, roe=0.9).
notes: Define errors out of existence, inverted (APOSD 9/16): the parser is meticulous about hostile input (token caps, nesting caps, chained-comparison rejection at 321-328) and then admits a boolean where a number belongs, because _is_boolean (449) inspects only the ROOT node while _call (388) parses each argument as a full _or_expr. The evaluator's float(a) at 513 turns the category error into a plausible-looking number, so the user or an agent gets a wrong screen instead of a positioned FormulaError - the opposite of the recovery-first contract the module advertises. Note the TS twin already threads per-production boolean-ness (screener-expr.ts:249-325 returns isBool from every production) - two hand-mirrored parsers using structurally different validation strategies is itself the parity risk. Smallest fix: port the TS twin's per-production boolean flag into _Parser and reject a boolean operand in _call/_sum/_term/_factor.

title: matched_criteria is computed, shipped on the wire, read by nothing, and is always empty under a group
repro: Any run with group present (i.e. the builder's 'match ANY' mode, src/store/screener.ts:362-364) returns every row with matched_criteria: [] because apply_criteria only fills passed_indices on the flat branch. No frontend file reads the field, so the defect is latent rather than visible.
notes: Dead weight plus a trap (APOSD 1/17). The engine carries index-tracking machinery through its hottest loop for a consumer that does not exist, and host-actions.ts:1155-1156 flattens an agent's nested group into the flat criteria list specifically 'so older readers + the match-index column resolve' - preserving a behaviour for a column no file renders. Consequence: two subsystems pay upkeep for a phantom, and the first person to build the match-index column will ship it silently blank in ANY mode. Smallest fix: delete matched_criteria from ScreenerResultRow, types/screener.ts and apply_criteria, and drop the flattenLeaves mirroring in host-actions.ts; if the column is genuinely wanted, populate it on the group path first.

title: Enrichment phase swallows every exception as 'field missing' and stalls its own progress bar on failure
repro: A provider-adapter bug that raises AttributeError inside get_fundamentals during phase E produces the same observable outcome as a network timeout: every survivor reports missing_field:<f>, nothing above DEBUG is logged, and the 'enriching fundamentals n/m' line freezes because emit is only reached on the success path.
notes: except (TimeoutError, Exception) is a tautology - TimeoutError IS an Exception - and the redundancy signals the author meant to enumerate the expected failures and then gave up (APOSD 9/16). Consequence: the one systematic failure mode a maintainer most needs to see (the adapter is broken for every symbol) is indistinguishable from the one they expect (upstream is slow), and the phase reports partial progress forever. Smallest fix: catch (TimeoutError, ProviderError) for the expected cases, log anything else at WARNING, and move done += 1 / emit(...) into a finally so the bar advances on failures too.

title: Saved-screen deserializer hand-validates the shapes the server would catch and waves through the ones it would not
repro: A workspace blob with {name:'x', universe:'russell2000', criteria:[{field:'pe_ratio', operator:'approx', value:5}]} passes deserializeSavedScreens, loads into the draft on click, and fails at Run with a raw Pydantic 422 in the error banner.
notes: Complexity pushed upward, not down (APOSD 7): 60 lines walk the nested group's shape by hand while universe is accepted on typeof === 'string' and cast at 131, and criteria on 'field' in c alone. The validation is theatre at exactly the boundary that matters - a restored workspace is untrusted input. A validated universe set already exists one module over (_SCREENER_UNIVERSES, host-actions.ts:1150). Smallest fix: validate universe against that shared set and criteria against the discriminated operator union; that also makes the bespoke group walker mostly redundant.

title: India master accessors pass positional tuples across module functions; a reorder silently mislabels scrip_code as ISIN
repro: design - _bse_lookup returns (name, group, code, isin) and india_symbol_meta reads bse_row[2] as scrip_code, bse_row[3] as isin, bse_row[1] as group. Swapping two fields in the _bse_lookup comprehension type-checks, passes lint, and yields an ISIN in the scrip_code slot.
notes: Information leakage (APOSD 4): the tuple layout is knowledge shared by four call sites with nothing holding it. The blast radius is not cosmetic - market_cap_witness._lookup gates the entire non-provider share-count witness on scrip_code being a truthy string (market_cap_witness.py:123-125, 'NSE-only enrichment row -> share count is a yfinance backfill'), which is the guard that keeps the witness from reintroducing circularity. A silent swap either disables the witness for every name or feeds it an ISIN. Smallest fix: make _nse_rows/_bse_rows/_bse_lookup return NamedTuples - a one-line change per function, and every positional read becomes a named one.

title: sector_map_generated / sector_map_coverage bypass the lru_cache their sibling uses and re-parse the ~1 MB master on every call
repro: market_cap_witness._lookup calls sector_seed_for (cached) and then sector_map_generated (uncached) for EVERY witnessed Indian symbol, so each witness lookup re-reads and re-json-parses india_sector_map.json from the package resources.
notes: Inconsistency inside one module (APOSD 15/18): three functions read the same file, one is @lru_cache(maxsize=1) and two are not, with no comment explaining the split. It also makes a neighbouring comment false - market_cap_witness.py:109-111 says the blocking work is 'because the first call parses the ~1 MB map', which is true of line 120 and wrong about line 130 on every subsequent call. Consequence: a per-symbol megabyte JSON parse inside a to_thread that the research snapshot awaits. Smallest fix: @lru_cache(maxsize=1) on _load_master (all callers then inherit it) - one decorator, and reset_caches_for_tests gains one cache_clear.

title: ScreenerPanel recomputes three ledger aggregates twice per render, on every SSE progress frame
repro: Run india-all: each sweep chunk emits a progress frame, the panel re-renders (it subscribes to progress), and basisLine()/skipBreakdown()/freshnessLine() each run twice per render - skipBreakdown building a fresh Map over lastResult.skip_details (up to ~5,000 entries) both times.
notes:
Performance as design (APOSD 18) plus an avoidable idiom: `{fn() &&
{fn()}
}` calls fn twice by construction, in three places. The previous run's lastResult stays mounted for the whole of the next run (line 402), so the wasted work peaks exactly while the UI should feel live. Smallest fix: const basis = useMemo(basisLine, [lastResult]) (likewise the other two) and render the memo - three lines, no behaviour change.

title: Changing a numeric criterion's operator discards the threshold the user typed
repro: Set 'P/E < 8', change the operator dropdown to 'between' -> the criterion becomes {min: 0, max: 100}; change it to any scalar operator -> the value becomes 20. The typed 8 is gone with no undo.
notes: The value is orthogonal to the operator, so destroying it on an operator change is a special case with no justification (APOSD 16 - obviousness; the handler reads as if it were constructing a fresh criterion). Consequence: refining a screen - the thing a user does dozens of times per session - loses work every time the comparison direction changes. Smallest fix: carry the current scalar through (`value: 'value' in criterion && typeof criterion.value === 'number' ? criterion.value : 20`) and seed between from it (`{min: v, max: v}`).

title: runScreener duplicates the unary-fallback and run-completion protocol three times across 250 lines
repro: design - the 'POST /screener/run, set lastResult/status/error, null the abort slot, return' sequence appears at 402-420, at 424-442, and again in the stream tail at 551-564, each with its own isCurrent()/aborted ordering.
notes: Repetition where the duplicated thing is a protocol, not a value (APOSD 1/15). The superseded-run invariant is held by a seven-line comment at the top of the file (lines 30-36: 'every async path that reads this must capture it into a local controller ... guard every state write') - the structure could hold it instead, and a comment-held invariant spread over three copies is one careless edit from run B's state being clobbered by run A's cleanup. Smallest fix: one local `function finish(patch) { if (!isCurrent()) return; set(patch); _runAbortController = null; }` plus one `runUnary()` helper; the three blocks collapse to one line each and the invariant becomes structural.

title: Unreachable 400 handler on POST /screener/run whose comment teaches a false fact about the engine
repro: design - the route catches ValueError 'e.g. an unknown universe id is a ValueError in the engine'; resolve_universe raises ProviderError for both the unknown-id and custom-without-symbols cases, and universe is a Literal so FastAPI returns 422 before the engine is reached. Nothing can produce that 400.
notes: Comments describe non-obvious things correctly or not at all (APOSD 11/16). The handler is harmless; the comment is not - it tells the next maintainer that the engine signals bad input with ValueError, which will shape how they add the next error path. Smallest fix: delete the except branch and the comment, or make it honest about ProviderError -> 502.
